We want to finalize the connectivity approach for our Private deployment (VPC in us-west-2) and are weighing three patterns: VPC Peering, AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints), and a site-to-site VPN back to our on-prem estate. The main constraints from our side:

Tom / Sophie — thanks for the diagram and clear constraints. Below is a concise, operational recommendation and next steps. I tried to keep it short so you can paste into your MAS or runbook.

Summary recommendation (short):
- Preferred: AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for cross-account, managed access to Redwood Private control plane and inference endpoints when you want least blast radius and per-service access control. It gives the cleanest security boundaries and aligns well with our access-logging patterns.
- Alternative for very high throughput (same-account, same-region): VPC Peering (direct L3) reduces per-connection overhead and can be cheaper for sustained high egress if both VPCs are in the same region/account.
- Backup/DR: IPSec site-to-site VPN (or AWS Transit Gateway VPN attachments) as a resilient fallback across regions or as an encrypted path to on-prem. VPN is easier to get standing up quickly but has higher variance in latency and requires monitoring/HA appliances for production-grade SLAs.

Tradeoffs (short bullets):
- Security/audit: PrivateLink provides endpoint-level control and AWS flow logs + PrivateLink logs can be tied to your SIEM. Peering relies on security group/route tables and is broader by default (wider attack surface). VPN provides encryption in transit to on-prem but adds NAT/BGP complexity for cross-VPC routing.
- Latency/perf: Peering typically has the lowest hop count and smallest tail latency, then PrivateLink, then VPN (VPN adds encapsulation and often variable e2e latency).
- Operational complexity: VPN > Peering > PrivateLink in terms of try-to-forget. PrivateLink shifts interface management to AWS, which reduces ops for you but can require more IAM/endpoint policy work.
- Cost model: Peering charges inter-AZ/regional transfer at data transfer rates; PrivateLink has per-hour endpoint + per-GB data processing; VPN has hourly appliance/throughput + data transfer. For sustained high-volume inference, peering in-region often wins on pure $/GB.

Recommended immediate actions for MAS / procurement checklist:
1) Decide whether Redwood will be in the same AWS account and region as ACME inference VPC (same-account simplifies peering).
2) If cross-account, prefer PrivateLink and enumerate required IAM roles and endpoint policies.
3) For DR, request a Transit Gateway or managed VPN setup across regions with active health checks.
4) Capture target latency SLOs and run short perf tests (we can help run a lightweight latency harness).
5) We will provide a RedTeam-friendly network audit checklist (flow logs, endpoint logging, cert rotation) and the PrivateLink datasheet (attached).

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-minute follow-up tomorrow for the perf targets and to confirm account boundaries? I can loop in infrastructure leads.

Quick technical note / internal cc: Neha — I agree with the PrivateLink-first posture for cross-account. A couple of extra details for the MAS/doer notes:

- If ACME expects sustained >10 Gbps steady-state between the inference VPC and Redwood (rare for single-tenant per-customer setups), peering or Transit Gateway makes sense to avoid the per-hour / per-GB PrivateLink charge.
- For latency-sensitive endpoints (99p < 100ms), ensure application-level keepalive and connection pooling on the client side — PrivateLink can add a small per-request amplification if you don't reuse connections.
- If we need to support multiple ACME regions, propose a hybrid approach: PrivateLink for control-plane requests + peering inside a region for heavy data egress, with VPN as DR. I'll draft a small network appendix for the MAS.

@Lauren — we should include a short pricing appendix: estimated $/GB delta between privateLink vs peering for this expected throughput. Also need product + SLA sign-off (Rishi) if we are promising cross-region failover >99.9.

Karthik
Head of Field Solutions, Redwood Inference
